prompt: Apply the supplied AT&T/Time Warner agreement clauses to explicitly SYNTHETIC closing scenarios. Assume the merger closes under these unchanged clauses; all holdings are eligible ordinary shares, with no appraisal, excluded shares, taxes, dividends or corporate-action adjustments. A is the contract's completed averaging-window price; P is the separate price used to mark delivered AT&T stock. Scenario A: A=$36, P=$34. Scenario B: A=$40, P=$42. Scenario C: A=$44, P=$40. Apply the contract's three-decimal exchange-ratio rounding, then value cash plus delivered stock. Per-target-share values represent a 1,000-target-share holding divided by 1,000, avoiding fractional-share settlement. For B, a synthetic desk pays $108 per target share and incurs $0.20 per target share of total other costs. Its sole objective is positive net settlement profit conditional on closing. Find the break-even P as a continuous price (do not round to an exchange tick), and report whether B meets the objective. For the hedge, A has already been fixed at $40: report the positive number of AT&T shares to SHORT against 1,000 target shares so a subsequent small change in P leaves the marked closing payoff unchanged. Scenario U is separate: only P=$40 is known; A is missing and may be any positive value. Determine whether consideration is unique and give tight per-target-share lower and upper bounds from the collar. Return prices/values to at least six decimals when non-terminating, booleans as JSON booleans, and quote the governing clauses for each output; separate clause quotes are allowed. These are conditional contract calculations using a 2026 observed-source cutoff, not actual historical market observations, a completion forecast or a recommended trade.
